fichas.title: Office building layouts, alignment, and access systems
fichas.summary: Compares single-, two-, and three-row office layouts and supply-core arrangements. Single-row layouts are generally uneconomical except with deep office rooms; two-row layouts are a common administrative solution, while offset two-row and three-row arrangements can organize supply cores and daylight. Large central supply zones are most practical in high-rise buildings. The page discusses daylight depth, lightwells, compass orientation, fixed service cores, and staircase spacing for escape access.

Building alignment
Coinpass orientation is variously
estimated. According to Rosenauer,
90% of all office buildings in the
USA have a main axis ENV, because
the deeply penetrating morning and
evening sun is a disturbance. Sun
from the south can be shaded more
easily with sun blinds. According
to Joedicke (---7 refs), the main axis
in the N/S alignment is to ensure
sunlight through all rooms. Northfacing rooms are acceptable only
for layouts without a corridor.
